\begin{finding}{major}{f:code-spine-declared-error-unconstrained-knowledge-theorem}{The declared error is unconstrained: the knowledge theorem has content only with a bound on \texttt{piopError}}
Severity: major (a statement cannot be stated as written: the headline's \enquote{except with probability \texttt{piopError I}} has no counterpart)

\fhead{Evidence}\texttt{piopError P := P.\allowbreak{}toDef.\allowbreak{}err} (\texttt{Compose.\allowbreak{}lean:149}); \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} →\allowbreak{} ℝ\allowbreak{}≥\allowbreak{}0} (\texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}lean:66}), declared by each phase; \texttt{Def.\allowbreak{}append} keeps each component's declaration (\texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}lean:148}). ArkLib's bound is \texttt{Pr[…] ≤ err i} (\texttt{RoundByRound.\allowbreak{}lean:568}) with no constraint on \texttt{err}. Probe \texttt{P4Junk.\allowbreak{}lean} (D.3 (b)): five phases that draw a challenge and check nothing, each declaring error \texttt{1}, inhabit \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Security toy}; both master theorems hold of them; \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} ∀\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} j\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{} =\allowbreak{} 1}. The construction is instance-independent. The blueprint's only bound, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} Σ\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} s\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{} ≤\allowbreak{} 2\allowbreak{} \textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{} 4\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} /\allowbreak{} |\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} +\allowbreak{} f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r} (\texttt{:1130}), is over an argument \texttt{s} the spine's \texttt{piopError} does not take, and the convention row \emph{Errors} (\texttt{:318}, \enquote{the closed form is a \texttt{def} next to the theorem, and the interactive error is its sum}) names no theorem.

\fhead{Classification}an error of the blueprint (an omission the spine inherited).

\fhead{Where the bound belongs}Two designs are consistent with the spine; the second is recommended.

\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{A field of \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Security}.} Add to \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Security} (or to a new structure \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Error}) a closed form \texttt{bound : ℝ≥0} and a proof \texttt{e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} ∑\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} P\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{} ≤\allowbreak{} b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d}, and restate the master theorem's docstring with it. Cost: one field, and each phase's \texttt{Security} must come with a bound on its own \texttt{D.\allowbreak{}err} (a lemma per phase, summed by \texttt{Def.\allowbreak{}append}). It keeps the errors declared by the phases, so a phase author still writes the closed form, and the bound is a hypothesis of the composition, not a consequence.
\item \emph{A closed form fixed by the spine.} Make the error a function of the \textbf{schedule}, not a declaration: \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Def.\allowbreak{}err} is removed; \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Security} carries \texttt{err} with its \texttt{rbr}; the spine states, per phase slot, the closed form leanVM's analysis gives (\texttt{4·2\textasciicircum{}\{μ\_\allowbreak{}bus\}/\allowbreak{}|E|} on \texttt{(\allowbreak{}α,\allowbreak{} β)} and \texttt{gkrError} for the bus, \texttt{(\allowbreak{}B+2)/\allowbreak{}|E|} and \texttt{3/\allowbreak{}|E|} per round for the table sumcheck, \texttt{1/\allowbreak{}|E|} for the public input, \texttt{flockError}, \texttt{(\allowbreak{}J−1)/\allowbreak{}|E|} and \texttt{2/\allowbreak{}|E|} per round for the opening; blueprint Layers 6 to 10), as a function \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} I\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} →\allowbreak{} ℝ\allowbreak{}≥\allowbreak{}0} of the instance's sizes, and \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Security} demands each phase's \texttt{rbr} \textbf{at that error}. Then \texttt{piopError I} exists as the headline writes it, \texttt{piopError\_\allowbreak{}le} is a theorem of the spine about the instance's sizes (provable now, by \texttt{norm\_\allowbreak{}num} at the caps once \texttt{leanIsaInstance}'s sizes exist), and a phase that cannot meet its slot's error has no \texttt{Security}. Cost: the schedules must then also be fixed by the spine (the error is indexed by the challenge), which the blueprint's convention \emph{Holes} leaves to each phase's \texttt{Def}; this is the same move the sibling dossier recommends for \texttt{BusOut}'s shape, and Layer 12's \texttt{verify} needs the schedules fixed anyway.
\end{itemize}

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{The declared error is unconstrained: the knowledge theorem has content only with a bound on \texttt{piopError}}
\asis (\texttt{:318}) \enquote{Errors | \texttt{ℝ≥0}, per verifier message, as ArkLib's \texttt{rbrKnowledgeError}; the closed form is a \texttt{def} next to the theorem, and the interactive error is its sum.}
\asproposed \enquote{Errors | \texttt{ℝ≥0}, per verifier challenge, as ArkLib's \texttt{rbrKnowledgeError}. The spine fixes the closed form of every phase's error as a function \texttt{piopError I} of the instance's sizes, and \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Security} demands each phase's round-by-round bound at that error; \texttt{piop\_\allowbreak{}rbrKnowledgeSoundness} is stated at \texttt{piopError I}, and \texttt{piopError\_\allowbreak{}le} bounds its sum at the caps. A phase may not declare its own error: with an unconstrained declaration the knowledge theorem holds of a protocol that checks nothing (declared error 1).}
\end{change}
Also \texttt{:1122} (\texttt{def piopError (\allowbreak{}s : Sizes)}) and \texttt{:1130} to be restated over \texttt{I}; and item 6 of \emph{What the spine fixes} (\texttt{:431-{}437}) to say that \texttt{piopError} is the spine's, not the phases'.


\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{minor}{f:code-spine-outputpure-field-redundant-guarded-nearly}{The \texttt{outputPure} field is redundant, and \texttt{guarded} nearly so}
Severity: minor (avoidable audit surface)

\fhead{Evidence}D.7, \texttt{outputPure\_\allowbreak{}of\_\allowbreak{}def}: every \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Def} over \texttt{[]ₒ} has a pure prover output, because no query is possible. ArkLib at the pin has the instance \texttt{Prover.\allowbreak{}instOutputIsPureEmpty} (\texttt{NoAmbient.\allowbreak{}lean:39-{}42}), not imported by the spine, and \texttt{Verifier.\allowbreak{}GuardedForm.\allowbreak{}ofEmpty} (\texttt{NoAmbient.\allowbreak{}lean:46-{}55}): every verifier over \texttt{[]ₒ} has a guarded form, given a fallback verdict for the rejecting branch. The field \texttt{outputPure} is one of the three of \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Complete} (\texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}lean:79-{}80}); every phase discharges it by \texttt{⟨\_\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} fun \_\allowbreak{} ↦ rfl⟩} (\texttt{PublicInput.\allowbreak{}lean:386}, \texttt{SendOracle.\allowbreak{}lean:78}, \texttt{PassThrough.\allowbreak{}lean:85}).

\fhead{Classification}a deviation forced by an upstream library, retired when the pin includes a module the spine can import.

\fhead{Proposed change}
Code: delete the field; \texttt{Complete.\allowbreak{}append} takes the instance. Keep \texttt{guarded}: the composed extractor names \texttt{G.\allowbreak{}out} (\texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}lean:178}), and a hand-written verdict is what an auditor reads, where \texttt{ofEmpty}'s is \enquote{run the verifier}. Blueprint \texttt{:505-{}507} and the sketch accordingly.

\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{note}{f:code-spine-instance-data-theorems-trust-nothing}{The instance is data the theorems trust, and nothing on \texttt{main} says any instance but the toy has an inhabited relation}
\fhead{Evidence}C.1 (\texttt{aux}), C.2 and D.4 (a \texttt{Layout} may alias columns; \texttt{toyAlias} has an empty relation and is an \texttt{M3Instance}); \texttt{Layout.\allowbreak{}read\_\allowbreak{}eval} is the only law an instance obeys. Nothing in the spine relates two instances or bounds what an instance may declare; the master theorems hold of every instance including the empty ones.

\fhead{Classification}a deliberate deviation (the wall), to be kept, with the theorem it owes named.

\fhead{Proposed change}
Blueprint, \emph{What the spine fixes} item 1 (\texttt{:412-{}414}): append \enquote{An instance is trusted data: the spine proves nothing about it beyond \texttt{read\_\allowbreak{}eval}, and the master theorems hold of instances whose relation is empty. For leanISA the instance is Category B (layouts, separators, count columns, lines) and its non-vacuity is \texttt{m3Holds\_\allowbreak{}stackOf} (Layer 3), its faithfulness Layer 12's fixture.}

\end{finding}

\subsubsection{Findings on the public-input phase}\label{sec:gen-findings-pubinput}

\par\noindent{\small\textit{Cross-references.} A reference such as \enquote{(D.5)} or \enquote{section B} in this part is to a section of the dossier \file{dossiers/code-pubinput.md}, whose codes the headings keep in parentheses: A (catalogue) is \cref{sec:gen-cat-pubinput}; B (faithfulness), E (the flag \lean{PublicLine.sent}) and F (statement checks) is \cref{sec:gen-conf-pubinput}; C (mutation probes) and D (the top limb) is \cref{sec:gen-probes-pubinput}; G (findings) is \cref{sec:gen-findings-pubinput}.}\par

Names in words; the earlier documents' codes in parentheses only where they locate a passage.

\begin{finding}{major}{f:code-pub-check-on-public-input-message}{The check on the public-input message is not load-bearing for any theorem of the phase (G.1)}
\fhead{Evidence}C.3 (the verifier with no check has \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Security} at the same error, no \texttt{sorryAx}), C.4 (for every message function and every check the message passes, \texttt{securityG}; instances with no check, with forty-two zeros, with the swapped check and a matching prover), C.5 (the first-value check; the words' equation). Root cause: \texttt{pooled} (\texttt{PublicInput.\allowbreak{}lean:127-{}128}) reads the statement, not the message; the message enters \texttt{check} and nowhere else; the proof of \texttt{rbr} (\texttt{:350-{}366}) never mentions \texttt{check}. The build the earlier review read pooled the values sent, and its item \enquote{H1: one output, \texttt{pooled}} (\texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}3}) removed the dependence, so the same review's table \enquote{each of five wrong verifiers breaks a stated theorem} (\texttt{:104-{}114}, rows (i) and (v)) stopped being true of the code as merged; the status repeats the claim (\texttt{protocol-{}status.\allowbreak{}md:440}).

\fhead{Consequence for the requirement}\enquote{A verifier that omits a check leanVM makes, or makes a weaker one, must have no proof of knowledge soundness} fails for this check, and no theorem about this phase as designed can restore it: the verifier without the check is knowledge sound. \enquote{A verifier that makes a wrong check must have no proof of completeness} holds only against a fixed honest prover (C.10); with the prover adapted to the wrong check both theorems hold.

\fhead{Classification}An error of the design (the blueprint's Layer 8 text describes a phase whose check ties the pool to the statement; the code's does not), introduced by an audit-surface compression.

\fhead{Proposed change}
Pool the values sent: replace \texttt{pooled} by \texttt{pooledFrom} (C.6, the definition is in \texttt{tools/\allowbreak{}lib.\allowbreak{}py}, with \texttt{pooledFrom\_\allowbreak{}expected} proved), in \texttt{verifier}, \texttt{prover.\allowbreak{}output}, \texttt{guarded.\allowbreak{}out} and the state function's rounds 1 and 2 (round 1 becomes \texttt{∃\allowbreak{} c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} s\allowbreak{} r\allowbreak{} c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} ∧\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} s\allowbreak{} r\allowbreak{} c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} ∈\allowbreak{} S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b}; with the per-limb check \texttt{cs} is forced to \texttt{expectedValues}, so \texttt{bad\_\allowbreak{}challenge\_\allowbreak{}unique} is unchanged). Then the check is load-bearing: its removal is refuted (C.6), its weakening is refuted (C.7), and a wrong check breaks completeness for every prover (C.10, last paragraph). Blueprint \texttt{:1035-{}1037}

\begin{change}{The check on the public-input message is not load-bearing for any theorem of the phase}
\asis For a line whose value was sent the value pooled is the value sent, since the check has just passed; for the others it is the value the verifier computes.
\asproposed For a line whose value was sent the value pooled is the value sent, as §8.2 and the pinned verifiers pool it; for the others it is the value the verifier computes. The check is what makes the pooled claims the statement's: without it the prover's values are pooled unchecked and the phase has no knowledge-soundness proof (test); a verifier that pools the values it computes would be knowledge sound with no check at all, which is why the pool must read the message.
\end{change}
Status \texttt{:440}: strike \enquote{each of five wrong verifiers breaks a stated theorem} or requalify it as a property of the build reviewed, not of the code merged. Tests: add, next to \texttt{threeLimbs}, the refutations of C.6 and C.7 as theorems (they are twenty lines each with the two lemmas of C.1, which belong in \texttt{ToArkLib/}).


\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{major}{f:code-pub-theorems-are-about-verifier-none}{The theorems are about a verifier none of the three executable verifiers runs, and the debt is assigned to a layer that cannot pay it (G.2)}
\fhead{Evidence}B.1: the specification checks per limb (\texttt{0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}1}); the Rust (\texttt{cpu/\allowbreak{}mod.\allowbreak{}rs:752-{}755}), the Python (\texttt{verifier.\allowbreak{}py:1400}) and the recursion guest (\texttt{aggregate.\allowbreak{}py:1681-{}1684}) check \texttt{c₀ + y·c₁ = w₀ + r·(\allowbreak{}w₀ + w₁)} and pool the scalars sent; the Lean is the specification's. The blueprint assigns the deployed check's soundness to Layer 12 (\texttt{:1053-{}1062}), whose theorem \texttt{verify\_\allowbreak{}iff\_\allowbreak{}compiled} (\texttt{:1218-{}1221}) cannot hold with a \texttt{verify} written from the Rust, and cannot detect the difference with a \texttt{verify} written per limb (the fixture is an honest proof). The status finding (F18) records the divergence correctly and draws the same wrong assignment (\texttt{:330}).

\fhead{Classification}A disagreement between the specification and its three implementations (a leanVM finding: an ambiguity of §8.2, not an unsoundness: the lemma of C.13 proves the implementations' check sound at \texttt{1/\allowbreak{}|E|}); the blueprint follows the specification, as a deliberate deviation from the deployed verifier, and owes the deployed verifier's theorem in the wrong place and in the wrong shape.

\fhead{Proposed change}
Layer 8 builds the deployed phase as well (B.1: \texttt{deployedVerifier}, \texttt{deployedPhase}, \texttt{deployedSecurity}, with \texttt{checkWords} of C.5 and \texttt{pooledFrom} of C.6; key lemma \texttt{accepts\_\allowbreak{}two\_\allowbreak{}challenges} proved in \texttt{ProbeWordsLemma.\allowbreak{}lean}), and the master theorems and Layer 12 consume it; the specification's phase stays with a one-line lemma that its acceptance implies the deployed one's. Blueprint \texttt{:1061-{}1062}

\begin{change}{The theorems are about a verifier none of the three executable verifiers runs, and the debt is assigned to a layer that cannot pay it}
\asis So the pinned verifiers accept transcripts this verifier rejects, their knowledge soundness at \texttt{1/\allowbreak{}|E|} is a lemma of its own, and Layer 12 owes it.
\asproposed So the pinned verifiers accept transcripts this verifier rejects. Their verifier is a second \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Def} on the same schedule (\texttt{deployedPhase}: the equation on the two words, the values sent pooled), with its own \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Security} at \texttt{1/\allowbreak{}|E|} (the two low limbs as one line through \texttt{E}, \texttt{accepts\_\allowbreak{}two\_\allowbreak{}challenges}); \texttt{Phases} and Layer 12 take the deployed phase, and the specification's is kept as the reference of §8.2 with the lemma that its acceptance implies the deployed one's.
\end{change}
Report to leanVM: §8.2 states two equations, the three implementations check one; both sound; choose.


\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{minor}{f:code-pub-top-limb-checked-instance-s}{The top limb is checked by the instance's third line and enforced by the adaptor's theorem, which is not built; the acceptance test names the wrong witness (G.3)}
\fhead{Evidence}D.1: every theorem of the phase and the spine is stated over an arbitrary \texttt{M3Instance}, so an instance with two lines has them all; \texttt{SatisfiedBy.\allowbreak{}word0\_\allowbreak{}eq} (\texttt{Statement.\allowbreak{}lean:338}) with \texttt{P\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} =\allowbreak{} E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}₀\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}₁\allowbreak{} 0} (\texttt{Memory.\allowbreak{}lean:107}) requires the top cell to be zero, and \texttt{satisfiedBy\_\allowbreak{}witnessOf} (blueprint \texttt{:815-{}816}) is what would be false without the third line; \texttt{constraintSoundness} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} follow. D.2: acceptance test 10's witness exists (\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}…\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}0}) but shows the pool, not the theorem, and on a toy-shaped instance.

\fhead{Classification}Not a divergence; an incomplete audit trail in the blueprint.

\fhead{Proposed change}
Acceptance test 10 (\texttt{:1293-{}1295})

\begin{change}{The top limb is checked by the instance's third line and enforced by the adaptor's theorem, which is not built; the acceptance test names the wrong witness}
\asis omitting it lets a non-canonical public word pass the line. Witness: the Layer 8 mutation with a nonzero \texttt{mem\_\allowbreak{}2} at cell 0 and the third claim dropped.
\asproposed omitting it lets a non-canonical public word pass the line. The phase and the spine cannot notice: an instance listing two lines has every one of their theorems. What fails is the adaptor's \texttt{satisfiedBy\_\allowbreak{}witnessOf}, at \texttt{SatisfiedBy.\allowbreak{}word0\_\allowbreak{}eq}, whose right-hand side \texttt{input.\allowbreak{}word0} has a zero top limb by type (\texttt{Memory.\allowbreak{}lean:107}). Witnesses: the Layer 8 test \texttt{threeLimbs} (the third claim rejects the stack \texttt{badTopLimb}; without it the stack passes), and, when Layer 3 lands, a \texttt{\#guard} that \texttt{(\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} s\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t} lists \texttt{mem\_\allowbreak{}2} with cells \texttt{(\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{} 0)} and \texttt{sent = false}.
\end{change}

\end{finding}

\fhead{Evidence}E: the theorems hold for every assignment; leanISA's \texttt{(\allowbreak{}true,\allowbreak{} true,\allowbreak{} false)} is in the blueprint's prose (\texttt{:834-{}836}, \texttt{:1037-{}1039}) and decision 15, with no definition (Layer 3) and no transcript fixture (Layer 12) yet.

\paragraph*{Negative results of the public-input dossier}

\begin{itemize}
\item The schedule, the challenge, the number of scalars, the point \texttt{(\allowbreak{}r,\allowbreak{} 0,\allowbreak{} …,\allowbreak{} 0)}, the honest values, the three claims and their order, the rejection, and the error agree between the specification, the three implementations and the Lean (table in B); checked line by line as cited there.
\item The bit order of \texttt{linePoint} is proved, not assumed (\texttt{eval₂Mle\_\allowbreak{}linePoint}), and separated from the other order by the test on a two-variable table (\texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}…:60-{}66}).
\item \texttt{1 + r} versus \texttt{1 -{} r}: joined by \texttt{CharTwo.\allowbreak{}sub\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}add} (\texttt{:182}), correct in characteristic two.
\item The error is charged to the right challenge and is tight (F).
\item No admitted ArkLib theorem in the closure of the two bundles (F, on the verbatim copy).
\item The knowledge state function's three rounds are the right ones and none is trivial (F; the bad event is inhabited, C.3's \texttt{rbr\textquotesingle{}} shows the same bound for the unchecked verifier).
\item \texttt{sent} is no part of the relation (E; \texttt{M3Holds} does not read it).
\end{itemize}

\par\noindent{\small\textit{Cross-references.} A reference such as \enquote{(D.5)} or \enquote{section B} in this part is to a section of the dossier \file{dossiers/code-layer1.md}, whose codes the headings keep in parentheses: A (catalogue) is \cref{sec:gen-cat-layer1}; E (audit surface) is \cref{sec:gen-surface-layer1}; F (conformance) is \cref{sec:gen-conf-layer1}; G (findings) is \cref{sec:gen-findings-layer1}; I (probes) is \cref{sec:gen-probes-layer1}; B (faithfulness), C (statements), D (the wall and the To-folders) and H (the upgrade) is not reproduced in these fragments; they are in the dossier.}\par


\begin{finding}{major}{f:code-l1-strided-reader-eighteen-blake2s-limb}{The strided reader of the eighteen BLAKE2S limb columns exists nowhere and is assigned to no layer (G.1)}
Severity: major (the blueprint omits something leanVM does, and \texttt{leanIsaInstance} cannot be built without it).

\fhead{Evidence}leanVM reads the limb columns as strided slots of \texttt{q\_\allowbreak{}flock} (\texttt{pcs/\allowbreak{}src/\allowbreak{}stack\_\allowbreak{}open.\allowbreak{}rs:84-{}97}; \texttt{py:884-{}894}, \texttt{P\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}…\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} Q\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{})} with \texttt{low = 8}; \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}5}; \texttt{gt-{}flock-{}ring.\allowbreak{}md} 2.4, 5.4). Layer 1 has only high-index selection (\texttt{slice}, \texttt{evalMle\_\allowbreak{}append\_\allowbreak{}boolVec}, \texttt{unstack}), and says so (\texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}1}). \texttt{Layout.\allowbreak{}comap} cannot place a limb column: its height \texttt{2\textasciicircum{}τ\_\allowbreak{}B} is no block's (B.8). The blueprint's Layer 3 (\texttt{:841-{}848}) says the instance \enquote{combines the two} readers but no layer sketches the selection lemma, the strided reader or the combinator; the slot map is placed in Layer 9's \texttt{FlockInterface.\allowbreak{}limbColumns} (\texttt{gt-{}flock-{}ring.\allowbreak{}md} 8.2). \texttt{StridedProbe} proves the missing generic lemma in twenty lines from Layer 1's own lemmas.

\fhead{Classification}an error of the blueprint (omission).

\fhead{Proposed change}
In the Layer 1 sketch, after \texttt{evalMle\_\allowbreak{}append\_\allowbreak{}boolVec}, add:

\begin{quote}
\begin{leancode}
def sliceLow (t : CMlPolynomialEval R (k + m)) (i : Fin (2 ^ k)) : CMlPolynomialEval R m
theorem evalMle_boolVec_append (t) (i) (s) : evalMle t (boolVec i ++ s) = evalMle (sliceLow t i) s
-- Stack.lean
def Blocks.stridedLayout (hμ) (b : Fin B.n) (k : ℕ) (slot : ι → Fin (2 ^ k))
    (h : ∀ c, B.size b = k + κ c) : Layout μ ι κ       -- column c = sliceLow of block b at slot c
def Layout.piecewise (L₁ : Layout μ ι₁ κ₁) (L₂ : Layout μ ι₂ κ₂) : Layout μ (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂) (Sum.elim κ₁ κ₂)
\end{leancode}
\end{quote}

and in the prose: \enquote{leanVM reads the eighteen BLAKE2S limb columns as strided slots of \texttt{q\_\allowbreak{}flock}: the low eight coordinates of \texttt{q\_\allowbreak{}flock}'s block are frozen to the slot's bits (\texttt{stack\_\allowbreak{}open.\allowbreak{}rs:84-{}97}). \texttt{evalMle\_\allowbreak{}boolVec\_\allowbreak{}append} is the low-index selection identity; \texttt{Blocks.\allowbreak{}stridedLayout} packages it as a \texttt{Layout}, and \texttt{Layout.\allowbreak{}piecewise} joins it to the aligned layout; Layer 3 transports the sum type to \texttt{ColumnId}.} Tests: the slot's strided slice against the aligned slice of the same index; a limb claim's lifted point against \texttt{Placement.\allowbreak{}stack\_\allowbreak{}point} of \texttt{py:295-{}297} on the layout of \texttt{offsets.\allowbreak{}py}. Reason: without it the instance's \texttt{layout} cannot be written, and the Rust's \texttt{Strided} claims have no Lean counterpart.

\end{finding}

\begin{finding}{major}{f:code-l1-leanisainstance-fits-cannot-be-stated}{\texttt{leanIsaInstance\_\allowbreak{}fits} cannot be stated as written, and is needed before the instance, not after (G.2)}
Severity: major by the scale's letter (a statement that cannot be stated as written); the fix is one line.

\fhead{Evidence}\texttt{protocol-{}blueprint.\allowbreak{}md:808}: \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} s\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} ≤\allowbreak{} 2\allowbreak{} \textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} s\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}μ}. \texttt{Layout} has the fields \texttt{read}, \texttt{extend}, \texttt{read\_\allowbreak{}eval} only (\texttt{Spine/\allowbreak{}Instance.\allowbreak{}lean:73-{}81}); \texttt{total} belongs to \texttt{Blocks} (\texttt{Stacking.\allowbreak{}lean:87}), and \texttt{Blocks.\allowbreak{}layout} takes the fit as its argument \texttt{hμ} (\texttt{Stack.\allowbreak{}lean:97}), so the instance's \texttt{layout} field cannot be filled until the fit is proved.

\fhead{Classification}an error of the blueprint.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{\texttt{leanIsaInstance\_\allowbreak{}fits} cannot be stated as written, and is needed before the instance, not after}

The earlier review marked the matter \enquote{Met in the documentation … the instance (I2) supplies it} (\texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}4}). The leaf stacks have the same gap (\texttt{gt-{}bus.\allowbreak{}md} G7).

\fhead{Classification}an error of the blueprint (a check deferred with no witness named).

\fhead{Proposed change}
Add to Layer 3's tests (\texttt{:866-{}867})

\begin{change}{The order of equal-size blocks is pinned by no statement, definition or test before the compiled verifier}
